extracted.intended_audience: general news audience (readers interested in corporate crisis, social media, and brand reputation)
extracted.subtask_description: A news article reporting on a corporate reputational crisis caused by an employee-posted viral video, describing how social media spread the content and how the company and authorities responded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond swiftly using the same platforms the content spread on
rubrics_metrics.description: The company's swift response to the employees and its wider customer base, using the same Web sites and media that spread the video, has been praised by observers who nevertheless wonder if the company can emerge unscathed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same social networks and sites where harmful content circulated (e.g., Twitter, blogs, YouTube) to communicate quickly to customers and stakeholders. Speed is emphasized as key to limiting reputational damage; timeliness can be a factor in whether observers 'praise' the response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor social media and leverage public information/crowdsourcing to identify incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: The digital mob played a role in alerting the company to the errant employees and tracking down their identities. Readers of the consumer affairs blog consumerist.com... tracked Hammonds down through her YouTube account and identified the store from matching an exterior shot in a video with an image on Google maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively monitor blogs, YouTube, Twitter and other platforms for emerging issues; treat engaged users and consumer watchdogs as potential sources of investigative leads. Use publicly available account info and geographic clues (e.g., matching exterior shots to map imagery) to identify locations and personnel involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact local franchisees/operators immediately and instruct decisive remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: "By Tuesday, we had contacted the franchise owner, given him the info we had and told him to take quick and decisive action."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an incident involves a franchise location, corporate should promptly notify the franchise owner, provide information gathered, and direct immediate remedial steps. Clear, direct instructions to local management to 'take quick and decisive action' are presented as a necessary operational response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take immediate remedial operational actions (close, restaff, sanitize)
rubrics_metrics.description: The store at which they worked was shut down to be restaffed and disinfected, according to a company spokesman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational remediation may include temporarily closing the affected location, restaffing, deep cleaning/disinfection, and other measures to restore health/safety standards and customer confidence. Such visible steps can be part of demonstrating responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue legal accountability when laws are broken
rubrics_metrics.description: Setzer and his colleague Kristy Hammonds... both were arrested and charged with food tampering, a felony in North Carolina.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If employee conduct violates public health or criminal statutes, ensure law enforcement is involved and that appropriate charges or legal steps are pursued. Publicizing that legal actions have been taken may affect public perception of company accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and plan for the rapid reputational impact of viral content
rubrics_metrics.description: The videos had been viewed by millions of people, highlighting the power of social media to tarnish a 50-year-old brand virtually overnight. Domino's was the latest company to be on the wrong end of a 'Twitter storm,' a spontaneously formed digital mob that rapidly shares information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that user-generated viral content can cause swift and widespread brand damage; crisis plans should anticipate 'Twitter storms' and include rapid-response communication, monitoring, and remediation protocols. Failure to prepare for virality is an implicit anti-pattern illustrated by the incident.
